planting.note: Grow as a houseplant in bright, indirect light in a chunky, well-drained aroid mix; frost-tender and only reliable outdoors in zones 10-11.

directions: This slender-stemmed botanical variety of the familiar Swiss cheese plant produces thinner cataphylls, shorter internodes, and noticeably smaller, more finely fenestrated leaves than the standard type, reaching a climbable, fruiting size years sooner. Give it a moss pole or similar rough support so aerial roots can anchor and trigger the jump from small juvenile leaves to broad, deeply split adult foliage. Let the top few inches of chunky mix dry between waterings and keep it out of direct midday sun, which scorches the thin leaf blades. Because it matures compact and fast, it is the form most often sold simply as a smaller-growing 'Monstera' for tight indoor spaces and hanging baskets before it is trained upright.

common_name: Variegated Swiss Cheese Vine (Variegated Monkey Mask Plant)

planting.note: Grow in a hanging basket or on a totem in bright, indirect light; frost-tender and only reliable outdoors in zones 10-11.

directions: A chimeric sport of the fenestrated swiss cheese vine, this cultivar carries irregular cream-to-white sectors across its perforated leaves, with variegation intensity ranging from lightly flecked to nearly half-white on the same plant. Because the white tissue lacks chlorophyll, give it slightly brighter indirect light than plain green adansonii to keep growth vigorous, but still avoid direct sun, which scorches the pale patches. Prune back stems that revert to solid green to preserve the variegated pattern, and provide a moss pole or trellis to encourage the larger, more heavily fenestrated leaves typical of climbing growth. Steady warmth, high humidity, and a chunky, fast-draining mix that dries slightly between waterings keep this slower-growing form healthy.
